title: Quarterly orbit sync: microsessions + escalation matrix
summary: Working draft for the Q2 all-company alignment that replaces a single long all-hands with a series of short, role-targeted microsessions plus an explicit escalation matrix. Purpose: increase action orientation, reduce meeting fatigue, and give leaders lightweight comms artifacts tied to OKRs.
audience: All staff; primary owners: execs + team leads + product-ops + people ops
objectives: Surface top-3 company priorities and visible owner for each
Run 6x 20-minute microsessions across two weeks targeting engineering, product, go-to-market, support, and platform teams
Create and socialize a one-page escalation matrix so teams know where to route blockers post-sync
Collect at least 200 asynchronous questions and tag them to owners for follow-up
proposed-microsession-topics: Serving runtime: latency SLOs, Dedicated capacity roadmap, key milestones
Hosted API: pricing experiment and traffic shaping plans
Private deployments: regulatory gating and pilot timeline
Optimize toolkit: batching/caching beta lessons and quantization recommendations
Console & Rollouts: rollout heuristics, canary playbook, regression monitoring
Customer success: high-touch accounts and escalation patterns
session-format: 20 min total: 8 min signal from exec/lead (top metric + ask), 7 min concrete next steps / owner commitments, 5 min live clarifying questions. All sessions recorded; question queue open asynchronously (Slack thread + Mural board).
timing-and-schedule: Week 1: Tue 09:00 engineering microsession; Wed 15:00 product + console
Week 1: Thu 11:00 sales + CS quick alignment
Week 2: Tue 09:30 private deployments + security; Wed 10:00 optimize toolkit demo
roles-and-owners: Security & Private deployment owner: Priya Singh (security-and-compliance)
decision-points: Do we keep the rotated microsession model as the default for the next two quarters? (needed by 2025-03-15)
Which priority gets the company-level KPI badge on the dashboard? (exec decision)
Accept proposed escalation matrix levels and assign SLAs for each level
open-questions: How will we measure 'reduced meeting fatigue' — survey cadence or calendar footprint?
Do smaller teams need separate breakout microsessions or is cross-functional enough?
What is the fallback for urgent product incidents that occur during the asynchronous window?
risks-and-mitigations: Risk: Fragmented attendance -> Mitigation: time-zone stagger, recordings + one-pager summaries
Risk: Questions pile up untriaged -> Mitigation: triage rota (1x day) and tagging to owners immediately
Risk: Exec bandwidth constraints -> Mitigation: execs provide a 2-slide 'signal kit' template to lower prep time
heatmap-notes: High friction areas (derived from ops intake): Dedicated capacity onboarding, private deploy networking, and SLO observability
Quick wins: extend caching hint docs, publish a batching cookbook, add a Dedicated capacity status widget to console
escalation-matrix-summary: Three levels: L1 = team-level (24h), L2 = cross-team/product-ops (72h), L3 = exec/incident hotline (ASAP). Each level needs an owner, a primary Slack channel, and a Jira tag. Draft routing: L1 -> #team-ops, L2 -> #ops-escalations + JIRA-OPS, L3 -> #exec-oncall + pager rotation.
communication-artifacts: Exec signal kit: 2 slides + 3 metrics + 1 clear ask
Asynchronous Q&A board (Mural) and consolidated FAQ doc
next-steps: Finalize topic owners and session leads by 2025-02-21 (owners above)
Publish microsession templates and recording process by 2025-02-24
Open asynchronous Q&A on March 1 and assign triage rota
Pilot the escalation matrix with two live incidents during March support window
notes-to-self: Keep sessions tight. Encourage execs to treat their 8 minutes as a 'signal + ask' not a status dump. Track attendance vs. follow-up closure rate as our leading health metric.
